title: Timed completion of verification
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $S$ on input $x$ whose state is empty. Suppose that, on input $x$ followed by $u$, machine $V$ is halted after $T$ steps and has output the one-bit word $[b]$, for some bit $b$. Then every Boolean choice word $w$ of length $|x|+|u|+2+(T+1)$ makes the host machine, started from the guessing-phase configuration determined by $c$ and $u$, halt with output $[b]$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ and $V$ are finite deterministic Turing machines over Booleans
$c$ is a configuration of $S$ on input $x$
$V$ is halted after $T$ steps on input $x$ followed by $u$, with output $[b]$
$w$ is a Boolean word of length $|x|+|u|+2+(T+1)$
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines, $d$ a halted scheduler configuration on an input $x$, $u$ a guessed word, and suppose $V$ computes the single-bit output $b$ on $x\,u$ within $T$ steps. Then for every choice word $w$ with $|w| = |x\,u| + 2 + (T+1)$, running the host under $w$ from the guessing-phase configuration for $(d,u)$ halts with output exactly the one-bit string $b$.
